final_responses.text:
Written to `APPROACH.md`. Here's the useful part.

**The reference is structurally tighter than it looks, and it works.** Measured, not estimated: the body block is 10×8 at (3,6), the frame is *exactly* 2 pixels on all four sides, and that leaves an interior of exactly **6×4 = 24 cells** — 22 fill plus 2 eye pixels. The sprite is centred on both axes. Alpha is binary only.

**The one insight that should drive production:** at 16×16 with a 2-pixel frame, this aesthetic is a cell-exact template, not a drawing. The frame, islands and centring consume fixed coordinates; a variant's entire expressive surface is those 24 interior cells plus the antenna silhouette. And because each eye sits with a full 8-neighbour moat of teal — which is *why* it reads as an eye rather than as frame noise — accents are confined to a 4×2 sub-rectangle. So your frame choice buys a chassis look and costs an 8-cell usable face. That's a real constraint, not a defect; the reference already lives inside it comfortably.

**The old assessment is rejected on measurement, not preference.** It claimed a 2-px border at 16px makes eyes meet the contour — here they have a full 1-cell moat on every side. It proposed one connected component for all sprites — this drone measures 3 components under *both* 4- and 8-connectivity, and that separation is a choice you own. Its third proposal (lock the three colors) isn't substantively wrong, it's just unapproved, so it becomes your decision rather than an inherited rule. The packaged sources back the first two rejections: `semantic-clusters` names `eye` as a protected singleton cluster, and the corpus's own readability fixture is a 16×16 form with separated landmarks.

**Two things I could not do, stated plainly:** no PixelLab tools are wired into this session — only `pixl-local` — so the provider schemas I read are a dated documentation inventory (`live_discovery: false`), not live discovery. The missing capability is a connected PixelLab MCP server with credentials. And no engine import target has been named, so that acceptance criterion stays genuinely open rather than assumed.

I also wrote `inspection/small-separated-x16.png`, an upscaled viewing aid so the visual read was an actual observation. No PX2 state, no art, no provider calls.

**Your decision — palette scope.** It's the only blocker, and it blocks exactly one criterion (`I8`, palette membership):

- **(a)** Fixed family palette — all drones use `#25354A` / `#56B5BC` / `#F4DDA2`.
- **(b)** Fixed *roles*, per-variant colours — **my recommendation.** Lock dark-frame / body-fill / accent as roles; let each drone carry its own hues. Preserves what makes the reference read without freezing colours you never chose.
- **(c)** Open per asset — structure is the only contract, drop `I8`.

Optionally confirm the proposed interior budget (≤6 of 24 cells non-fill; the reference spends 2). Without an answer I'll hold it as proposed and flag overruns rather than reject them.

approach.text:
# Drone production approach — 16×16 separated-antenna drone

Status: **planning only.** No PX2 state was initialized or amended, no production art was
generated, and no provider was called. This document is the single deliverable.

## 1. What was actually inspected

| Input | How it was read |
| --- | --- |
| `small-separated.png` (sha256 `1c45c866f9d11ff57b055f4dacf1e47c8e71f2c99fd6b24f0cb4259ee40cbe5c`) | `pixl_asset_check`; exact RGBA grid dump; viewed natively and at 16× nearest-neighbour on a checker backdrop |
| `old-assessment.md` | Read in full; disposed of in §5 |
| `SESSION.md` | Read in full |

`inspection/small-separated-x16.png` is an integer-upscaled viewing aid produced this session,
not production art. It exists so the visual read below is an actual observation rather than an
inference from numbers.

## 2. Measured reference facts

All values below are measured, not estimated.

```
   0123456789012345          A = #25354A  frame/dark   64 px
 0 ................          B = #56B5BC  body fill    22 px
 1 ................          C = #F4DDA2  accent/eye    2 px
 2 .....AA..AA.....          . = alpha 0            168 px
 3 .....AA..AA.....
 4 ................          canvas        16 × 16
 5 ................          visible       88 px, 3 colors
 6 ...AAAAAAAAAA...          alpha values  {0, 255} only — no fractional edge
 7 ...AAAAAAAAAA...
 8 ...AABBBBBBAA...
 9 ...AABCBBCBAA...
10 ...AABBBBBBAA...
11 ...AABBBBBBAA...
12 ...AAAAAAAAAA...
13 ...AAAAAAAAAA...
14 ................
15 ................
```

- **Body block** `x3..12` × `y6..13` — 10 w × 8 h.
- **Frame thickness measured on all four sides: exactly 2.**
- **Interior** `x5..10` × `y8..11` — 6 × 4 = **24 cells**, of which 22 fill + 2 accent.
- **Antenna islands** 2×2 at `(5,2)` and `(9,2)`. Vertical gap to body = 2 rows (4, 5);
  horizontal gap between islands = 2 columns (7, 8).
- **Component count is 3 under *both* 4- and 8-connectivity.** The separation is not a
  connectivity-rule artifact; it survives either rule with a clear margin.
- **Eyes** at `(6,9)` and `(9,9)`. Each has a *complete 8-neighbour ring of body fill* — neither
  accent cell touches the frame, diagonally or orthogonally.
- **Centred both axes**: margins L/R 3/3, T/B 2/2.

Visual read at 16×: the two islands read unambiguously as a separated antenna pair; the thick
frame reads as a chassis bezel rather than an outline; the two accent cells read as eyes because
of the moat, not because of their shape.

## 3. Authority ledger

| Choice | Authority | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16×16 canvas | **Confirmed by user** | 16 × 16 |
| 2-px dark frame around the body | **Confirmed by user** | thickness 2, all sides |
| Two detached antenna islands | **Confirmed by user** | 2 islands, non-touching |
| Frame / fill / accent *roles* | Proposed (derived from reference) | 3 roles |
| Specific hexes `#25354A` / `#56B5BC` / `#F4DDA2` | **Unknown — user has not approved a palette** | measured from this reference only |
| Interior detail budget | Proposed | see §4, ≤ 6 of 24 cells |
| Engine import behaviour | Unknown — untested | — |

Nothing in the "proposed" or "unknown" rows is treated below as settled. §7 carries the one
decision that actually blocks further work.

## 4. The production template

At 16×16 with a 2-pixel frame, this aesthetic is **not a drawing, it is a cell-exact template**.
That framing is the core of the approach: the frame, the islands, and the centring consume fixed
coordinates, and everything a variant can express lives in 24 interior cells plus the antenna
silhouette.

**Fixed geometry (every drone in the family):**

```
body block      (3,6) size 10×8        frame ring   2 px, dark role
interior        (5,8) size  6×4        = 24 cells, fill role
antenna A       (5,2) size  2×2        antenna B    (9,2) size 2×2
island gap      ≥2 rows to body, ≥2 cols between islands
placement       centred: margins 3/3 horizontal, 2/2 vertical
alpha           binary only (0 or 255)
```

**Variation surface (what a new drone may change):**

1. The 24 interior cells — eye position/count, a mouth or vent row, a chest indicator.
2. Antenna island *shape*, within a 2×2..2×3 footprint that preserves the ≥2-cell gaps.
3. Accent colour per variant, if §7 resolves that way.

**Proposed interior budget: at most 6 of 24 interior cells may be non-fill (25%).** The reference
spends 2 (8%). This ceiling is a proposal, not a measured threshold — it exists so variants are
compared against a declared number instead of being argued case by case. Confirm or replace it.

**Proposed moat rule (derived from the reference, and the reason the face reads):** every accent
cell keeps a full 8-neighbour ring of fill. With a 6×4 interior this confines accents to the
4×2 sub-rectangle `x6..9` × `y9..10`. That is a hard consequence of the user's own frame
choice and is worth stating plainly: **the 2-px frame buys a chassis look and costs an 8-cell
usable face.** It is a real constraint, not a defect, and the reference already works within it.

## 5. Disposition of `old-assessment.md`

The prior assessment was written against a *different* 32-px robot and was never approved. Each
of its three proposals is measurably wrong for this drone:

| Prior proposal | Measured result on this drone | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 32-px minimum whenever outlines are thick | A 2-px frame at 16 px leaves a working 6×4 interior; the eyes sit with a full 1-cell fill moat and **do not meet the contour** | **Reject.** The stated failure mode does not occur here. |
| One connected component for all sprites | Component count is 3 under both connectivity rules — and the detached islands are a user-confirmed aesthetic | **Reject.** Adopting it would delete a choice the user owns. |
| Lock all props to the observed three colors | The user has not approved any palette | **Do not adopt.** Not wrong in substance, but unapproved; it is §7's decision, not an inherited rule. |

The packaged sources agree that the first two are overreach. `semantic-clusters` records that
"a semantic cluster need not be a single-color connected component" and that "automatically
deleting every singleton destroys legitimate detail" — the two 1-px eyes are exactly the
protected singletons it describes, and `eye` is a named cluster semantic in
`PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md:1402-1445`. `palette-contract` records that "a fixed small palette is
optional art direction, not a universal definition of pixel art." The `silhouette-readability`
proof fixture is itself a **16×16** form with a ring hole and two separated teeth, i.e. the
corpus treats separated landmarks at 16 px as workable.

Carry forward from the prior note only this: thick frames at small canvases do squeeze interiors.
That is handled explicitly by the §4 budget rather than by a blanket size floor.

## 6. Method, in order

**Spine — author deterministically from the template.** Emit the fixed geometry directly, then
paint the interior and antennas. This is the recommendation because the aesthetic is defined by
exact cell coordinates; no generator can be relied on to land a 2-px ring and two ≥2-cell gaps at
16×16. Verify with `pixl asset-check` plus the §6.1 invariants.

**Exploration branch — use the provider for ideas, never for deliverables.** `create_1_direction_object`
with `style_images: [small-separated.png]`, or `create_image_pixen` at 16×16, to propose interior
motifs and antenna silhouettes. Then *conform* mechanically: snap the frame, re-separate the
islands, quantize to the approved roles. **Named risk:** at 16×16 these tools typically return a
connected, antialiased, many-colour raster. `reduce_colors` and `correct_pixelart` exist but
neither guarantees a 2-px ring or island separation. Budget for the conform step, or skip the
branch entirely — the spine does not depend on it.

**Provider availability — blocked this session.** No PixelLab tools are present in this session;
only `pixl-local` is wired. The tool list I read is a *dated documentation inventory*
(`retrieved_at: 2026-09-11`, `live_discovery: false`), not live discovery, so the schemas above
must be re-discovered against the real harness before any `job-prepare`. **Missing capability:
a connected PixelLab MCP server with credentials.**

### 6.1 Acceptance criteria — declared now, before any candidate exists

*Mechanical* (scriptable; these are the §2 measurements turned into assertions):

- `I1` canvas exactly 16×16; alpha values ⊆ {0, 255}.
- `I2` exactly 3 opaque components under **both** 4- and 8-connectivity: two antenna islands and
  one body, no island touching the body.
- `I3` frame thickness exactly 2 on all four sides of the body block.
- `I4` interior exactly 6×4 = 24 cells.
- `I5` every accent cell has a full 8-neighbour ring of fill.
- `I6` centred: margins 3/3 horizontal, 2/2 vertical.
- `I7` interior non-fill cells ≤ 6 *(pending §4 confirmation)*.
- `I8` palette membership *(cannot be authored until §7 resolves)*.

*Visual* (host inspection, not inferable from the above): native scale plus integer upscale, on
light, dark and busy backgrounds; confirm the islands still read as antennas and the accents still
read as eyes. Mechanical passes do not supply this verdict.

*Engine*: **untested and currently unknown.** No import target has been named, so no engine
criterion can be written yet. It stays open rather than being quietly assumed to pass.

## 7. The decision I need from you

**Is the palette fixed, and at what scope?** Everything else in this approach is executable; this
is the only item that blocks work, and it blocks exactly one thing — criterion `I8`. I cannot
author a palette check without it, and I will not infer approval from the reference's contents.

- **(a) Fixed family palette** — all drones use `#25354A` / `#56B5BC` / `#F4DDA2`. Strongest
  consistency, no per-variant colour expression.
- **(b) Fixed roles, per-variant colours** *(my recommendation)* — the three *roles* (dark frame,
  body fill, accent) are locked and `I8` checks role count and transparency, while each drone may
  carry its own accent or fill hue. This preserves what makes the reference read — thick dark
  bezel, one fill, one high-value accent — without freezing hues you have not chosen.
- **(c) Open per asset** — structure is the only contract; `I8` is dropped.

Reply with (a), (b) or (c). If you also want to confirm or replace the §4 interior budget of
6 of 24 cells, that turns `I7` from proposed into confirmed; absent an answer I will hold it as
proposed and flag any variant that exceeds it rather than rejecting it.
